scheme_name: Chief Minister’s Girl Child Protection Scheme-II
description:
The Chief Minister’s Girl Child Protection Scheme-II is a welfare initiative launched by the Government of India aimed at ensuring the welfare and empowerment of girl children in the state of Haryana.

This scheme was officially launched on 20th January 2016 as a continuation of the earlier Chief Minister’s Girl Child Protection Scheme-I which was initiated in 2005.

The primary objective of the scheme is to improve the sex ratio in Haryana which has been historically low.

As per the 2011 Census, Haryana had a sex ratio of 879 females for every 1000 males.

The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to families for the education and health of girl children.

The government has set a measurable target of increasing the sex ratio to at least 950 females for every 1000 males by the year 2025.

Under this scheme, families are provided with a financial incentive of ₹21,000 for the birth of a girl child.

This amount is deposited in the name of the girl child in a fixed deposit account.

The amount can be accessed by the family when the girl child reaches the age of 18 years.

In addition to the initial financial assistance, the scheme also provides for an annual scholarship of ₹5,000 for the girl child from the age of 6 to 18 years.

This scholarship is aimed at encouraging families to educate their daughters.

The eligibility criteria for this scheme include families residing in Haryana.

The family must have a girl child born on or after 20th January 2016 to qualify for the benefits.

There are no specific income criteria for eligibility under this scheme.

The application process for the Chief Minister’s Girl Child Protection Scheme-II is straightforward.

Families must fill out the application form available at the local Anganwadi centers or online on the official Haryana government website.

The required documents include the birth certificate of the girl child.

Families must also provide proof of residence in Haryana.

Additionally, a bank account in the name of the girl child is required for the disbursement of funds.

Once the application is submitted, it is verified by the concerned authorities.

The verification process typically takes about 30 days.

Upon successful verification, the financial assistance is credited to the bank account of the girl child.

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of health check-ups and immunizations for girl children.

Families are encouraged to ensure that their daughters receive regular health check-ups.

The government has partnered with various health departments to facilitate these health services.

The scheme also promotes awareness about the importance of girl child education.

Various workshops and seminars are conducted to educate families about the benefits of educating their daughters.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Department of Women and Child Development, Haryana.

The department can be contacted through their official website for any queries related to the scheme.

The scheme is part of a broader initiative by the Haryana government to empower women and girls in the state.

The government has allocated a budget of ₹100 crore for the implementation of this scheme for the financial year 2022-2023.

This budget is aimed at covering the financial assistance and scholarships for eligible families.

The scheme has seen a positive response since its launch.

As of 2023, over 1 lakh families have benefited from the scheme.

The government regularly monitors the implementation of the scheme to ensure that the benefits reach the intended beneficiaries.

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the scheme further.

The Chief Minister’s Girl Child Protection Scheme-II is a crucial step towards changing societal attitudes towards the girl child.

It aims to create a supportive environment for families to raise daughters without discrimination.

The scheme also aligns with the national Beti Bachao Beti Padhao initiative launched by the Government of India in 2015.

This national initiative aims to prevent gender-biased sex-selective elimination and promote the education of the girl child.

The Haryana government has been proactive in addressing the issues related to gender disparity.

The Chief Minister’s Girl Child Protection Scheme-II is one of the many initiatives aimed at ensuring gender equality.

The scheme has also contributed to raising awareness about the importance of the girl child in society.

The government encourages community participation in promoting the scheme.

Local self-help groups and NGOs have been involved in spreading awareness about the benefits of the scheme.

The scheme not only provides financial assistance but also aims to change mindsets regarding the value of girl children.

The government has also introduced various other schemes to complement the objectives of the Chief Minister’s Girl Child Protection Scheme-II.

These include schemes for women’s health, education, and employment.

The scheme is regularly reviewed and updated based on the changing needs of society.

The Haryana government is committed to ensuring that every girl child is given equal opportunities.

The Chief Minister’s Girl Child Protection Scheme-II is a testament to this commitment.

The scheme is expected to continue evolving to meet the needs of future generations.

Overall, the Chief Minister’s Girl Child Protection Scheme-II represents a significant effort by the Haryana government to empower girls and promote gender equality in the state.
